thread:
olivia: quick heads-up — ran an overnight long-run profile for INT8 KV cache using 50k long-context traces. seeing steady mem growth + a small but consistent recall drift on long-context retrievals. notes below.

devon: can you drop the tracer output / perf counters? nvprof or our runtime tracer output is fine.

olivia: pasted the relevant counters from runtime-trace (trimmed):
```
kv_slots.total=131072
kv_slots.used=89324
kv_fragmentation_pct=12.6
int8_pages=32768
page_faults=1200
reclaims=980
mem_usage_before=12.8GB
mem_usage_after=9.1GB
mem_savings=28.9%
eval/qa_f1_delta=-2.8%
```
(first_message = full 50k run; these are aggregate counters over 12h)

kai: interesting — mem savings look great, but 2.8% F1 drop is concerning. is the drop uniform or concentrated on certain prompt types?

olivia: concentrated on long-context entity resolution queries (>8k tokens). short prompts unaffected. trace-level inspection shows repeated eviction->rehydration loops for specific key prefixes. rehydration uses INT8 restore pipeline which seems to introduce small bias for certain attention heads.

ml-bench-bot: eval-suite/recall-longctx-2026-03-17: delta_f1 -2.8% (p=0.004). full diff: https://bench.internal/reports/recall-longctx-1841001234

devon: hypotheses: (1) eviction policy too eager for large keys causing churn on hot prefixes; (2) INT8 rehydrate quantization error amplifies over many kv reuses; (3) fragmentation causes partial-page restores that misalign KV chunks with GEMM kernels.

olivia: tried a quick patch (soft-evict + async-compaction) last night:
```
--kv.soft_evict=true
--kv.async_compact=true
```
Result: frag -> 4.2%, reclaims -> 240, mem stable over 12h, eval delta now -1.1% (still negative but improved).

kai: good signal. another angle is kernel selection: INT8 GEMM path uses 32x8 blocking vs BF16 64x16; if KV pages are rehydrated with different row alignment we may be hitting rounding differences at block boundaries. can you capture per-rehydrate checksum / head-wise residuals?

olivia: will add head-wise residual logs. initial spot check shows small skew in head 3/5 after rehydrate: mean delta ~0.6% relative to bf16 baseline. that matches the recall hits.

devon: operational mitigations to test in canary: (a) rehydrate-critical-keys-as-bf16 (store BF16 for top-k hot keys), (b) pin-hotset-percent=2, (c) keep-int8-for-cold. also add sampling-based rewarm on eviction to avoid immediate reaccess.

olivia: implementing plan. scheduled three canaries (staging A/B/C):
- A: bf16-topk=true, pin-hotset=2%
- B: soft-evict + async-compact (from last night)
- C: sampling-rewarm + improve page-rescue backoff

infra-bot: canary deploys triggered: staging-A (flags: kv_rehydrate_bf16=true, kv_pin_hotset_pct=2), staging-B (kv_soft_evict=true, kv_async_compact=true), staging-C (kv_sampling_rewarm=true). git: rfc/kv-int8-paging -> canary-3. run ids: canary-1841001245-1..3.

devon: nice. please also instrument: "rehydrate_precision" (enum), "page_rescue_latency_ms", and per-key "rehydrate_count". add an eval hook that runs the longctx recall suite every 6h while canary is active.

olivia: added instrumentation + gating. will upload the perf diffs and head-residual heatmaps after the first 6h canary window. thanks for quick triage :thumbsup:

kai: one more thought — we should try an INT8->BF16 hybrid rehydrate where we store small high-entropy subvectors in BF16 and rest in INT8. less memory hit than full BF16 but may recover most accuracy.

olivia: noted. will prototype hybrid store in the next experiment if canaries don't fully close the gap. current target: get F1 delta within +/-0.5% while keeping >=20% mem savings.

devon: sweet. schedule a quick eng-runtime sync tomorrow to decide rollout criteria.

olivia: ack — 10am PT. ending thread with logs uploaded to the run: s3://redwood-internal/kv-runs/1841001234/ (contains full tracer + head-residuals).
